Let me analyze the key features:
- White's king on g1 is vulnerable on the back rank
- Black has active pieces: queen on a5, rook on c8
- The White king has limited escape squares (blocked by pawns on e2, f2, h2)

**The winning move is Qe1+**

This forces checkmate in 2 moves:
- If 1...Qe1+ 2.Kh1 Rc1# (mate - king trapped with queen controlling g1)
- If 1...Qe1+ 2.Kf1 Rc1# (mate - king on f1 has no escape squares)

**Coaching Note:**
Your queen and rook can work together on the back rank. When you see the opponent's king trapped on the back rank with limited escape squares, look for a way to activate your queen with check, forcing the king into an even worse position. Then deliver checkmate with your rook on the first rank. This is one of chess's most powerful patterns—recognize these positions and you'll win games.
